text:
ana: heads-up — saw a sudden spike in ALB target deregisters in edge-us-east-1 at ~15:23UTC, lots of pods marked unhealthy.
ana: symptoms: ALB 504/timeout for /healthz then target removed after 2 failed checks :cry:
miguel: any recent deploys or config changes in that region?
ana: small rollout earlier but the pattern started ~20m after deploy and affected pods across multiple nodegroups, so thinking infra-level (conntrack / nat) rather than app regression
sasha: can you paste the ALB healthcheck log snippet and node conntrack stats?
ana: sure — ALB: "Target response timed out (connect timeout reached)" repeated
ana: on one affected node:
```
$ cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
126048
$ cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
131072
```
ana: conntrack sitting at ~96% of max on that node
ryan-oncall: that will definitely drop new connections. when conntrack is near-max you get silent drops which look like timeouts to ALB
miguel: what about kube-proxy / iptables churn? any restarts?
sasha: checked kube-proxy uptime: no recent restarts. but iptables-nat chain size is huge (many pod->external rules) from noisy egress workloads
ana: side note: our ALB healthchecks come from AWS IP ranges, but packets still traverse conntrack on the node and are subject to nf_conntrack exhaustion
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-348 — ALB target flapping in edge-us-east-1 (pagerduty)
ryan-oncall: short-term mitigation options:
- bump nf_conntrack_max on nodes
- reduce ALB healthcheck aggressiveness (increase timeout/interval) to avoid flapping while we stabilize
- scale NAT gateway / add more egress capacity
- consider switching kube-proxy to ipvs on next window to reduce conntrack pressure
miguel: agree. can we sysctl-bump on worried nodegroups first? do via daemonset with sysctl or use SSM to run on nodes
ana: I ran a quick sysctl on one node to confirm it helps:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
# conntrack_count dropped to ~85k after clearing some sockets
```
ana: after bumping, ALB targets started passing healthchecks again within ~60s for that node
sasha: good verification. still need cluster-wide fix — we're seeing ephemeral port pressure combined with lots of short-lived outbound connects from some batch jobs
ryan-oncall: action items:
- (P0) deploy daemonset to set nf_conntrack_max=262144 across edge-us-east-1 nodes (ryan)
- (P1) identify noisy egress workloads and throttle/queue them (miguel + sasha)
- (P2) schedule kube-proxy ipvs migration test (eng-infra)
- (P2) evaluate NAT gateway scaling vs. per-node SNAT map offload (cloud infra)
ana: also recommend temporarily changing ALB target group healthy threshold from 2 -> 3 and increasing timeout from 5s -> 10s to avoid immediate evicts while we stabilize
miguel: logging the change in infra runbook and will coordinate the daemonset rollout. leaving the ALB threshold change as manual — doing it after the daemonset push
sasha: ran `conntrack -S` and saw heavy TCP CLOSE_WAIT counts on a couple nodes — will investigate which pods are holding sockets
ana: FYI I rolled a single node kubelet after the sysctl bump to make sure nothing breaks — no regressions so far
ryan-oncall: good. i'll keep the pagerduty on until nodegroup daemonset is finished and we see stable healthy counts for 30m
infra-bot: update: INC-2026-348 assigned to eng-infra team. related runbook: /runbooks/conntrack-snat-exhaustion.md
miguel: note for post-mortem: add telemetry to detect nf_conntrack utilization and fire an alert at 80% to preempt flapping
ana: +1 — adding to follow-up. will post a summary in #eng-ops when done
sasha: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ryan-oncall: closing the loop here — keeping watch for next 1h and we'll pivot if anything else pops up
